question: Can the two interrupted original L1 experiments continue from preserved full-state checkpoints without changing their scientific protocol or endangering the four advancing originals?
hypothesis: The original trainer's full-state resume path can restore the saved step, model, head, optimizer, scheduler and RNG. Serial execution removes concurrent trainers but is not a demonstrated remedy for the unresolved GPU wait.

sources.sections: General checkpoint for resuming training, multiple models, GPU checkpoint loading on CPU
sources.consequence: Preflight all saved components against the original implementation, preserving the source artifact. A weights-only load is insufficient for resumption.

sources.sections: Reproducibility limitations, RNGs and nondeterministic algorithms
sources.consequence: Restore CPU/GPU RNG and retain the same environment and deterministic per-epoch/per-step seeds. Do not promise bitwise identity or change backend determinism settings mid-experiment.

sources.version: current official documentation read 2026-11-15; installed psutil 7.2.2
sources.sections: Process identity, is_running, terminate, kill and wait
sources.consequence: Bind any approved process action to PID plus creation time and command/cwd. Treat zombies and absent processes distinctly; never signal a reused PID.

On the same GPU model, a different runtime/workload reports device resets during hung-process teardown. Wait until healthy peers finish and their final artifacts are preserved before any process cleanup. This report does not diagnose our hang or authorize its workaround.

differences: Operational continuation of original n1/n3 L1 seed0 experiments, not a new model comparison. The interruption has already occurred. Source stays at 7dfc837, configuration/data/total303000 steps stay fixed; output directories and process concurrency change. CPU preflight is deserialization/state restoration only, with no training or model forward/backward.
contrary_evidence: A complete checkpoint does not prove that GPU recovery will work, that prior updates were numerically valid, or that resumption is bitwise equivalent. The GPU may require device-level recovery, which is outside this protocol. A stalled process may resume spontaneously. Four peers advancing contradict a wholly unusable GPU.

protocol.preparation: Verify A004 review and immutable recovery-asset digests. On CPU with GPUs hidden, load both step105000 checkpoints using original source, restore AdamW and LambdaLR, verify exact state and configuration, restore CPU RNG, inspect saved GPU RNG without initializing CUDA, verify finite floating state, and hash the existing train/validation data. Copy checkpoint/config/metrics to separate recovery directories only after both preflights pass. Record exact commands, source hashes, data hashes and checkpoint lineage. No signals or training during preparation.
protocol.authorization: Execution is pending an explicit user-approved exception to preserving the original process lifetimes and PID-bound A003 queue. This record does not grant that exception. Preparation and read-only monitoring are already in scope.
protocol.readiness: All four advancing original process identities have exited, and their matching final model.pt at303000 plus checkpoints/logs have been verified and preserved. Both affected processes still match captured identity/cwd/command and have unchanged metric step/checkpoint digest for at least15 minutes. If either resumes useful progress, cancel automatic recovery and reassess. Verify no other GPU trainer is active.
protocol.queue_retirement: Preserve the original A003 manifest/state/log and verify its source/config hashes. If it is still only waiting, terminate that identified CPU queue and confirm exit before stopping an original trainer. If already running diagnostics, stop this recovery procedure and reassess; never race a replacement with the old queue.
protocol.cleanup: After authorization and readiness only, use identity-checked SIGTERM for the two affected processes, waiting up to30 seconds each. If still present, one identity-checked SIGKILL is allowed by the proposed exception, then wait up to30 seconds. Retain before/after runtime and kernel observations. No GPU reset, reboot, driver/runtime changes or security-policy changes; if contexts do not exit or device faults appear, stop for a new reviewed decision.
protocol.continuation: Resume n1 then n3, one at a time, from immutable step105000 copies in outputs/balls/recovery_A005. Use the original Python environment, pinned checkout, seed0 and unmodified trainer/config/data. The original trainer trims only cloned metric rows beyond the saved step. Verify hashes immediately before each launch and record process identity, runtime, exit outcome and final artifacts. Do not silently retry a repeat stall or change hyperparameters/backends. Review each result before launching the next recovery or downstream diagnostic.
protocol.final_checks: After successful completion, resolve four original final paths plus two recovery final paths in a lineage index. Verify all six final steps/configs and preserved queue source. Execute the unchanged A003 numerical suite sequentially from its pinned checkout, then literature-review each result before any dependent research. Retain original interrupted evidence and document the queue replacement separately.
protocol.verification: Actual CPU loading/restoration checks and artifact hashes are the preparation evidence. No CPU optimizer update or GPU launch. Execution success requires final artifact verification and later A003 numerical validity; preparation alone cannot pass those gates.

success: Preparation: both complete saved states restore under original code and byte-identical isolated recovery inputs are ready. Execution: both original experiments reach303000 with finite final state and explicit lineage, followed by reviewed A003 validity. Report these as separate outcomes.
stop: No execution without approval/readiness; cancel if original progress resumes. Stop on changed source/config/data/checkpoint, process-identity mismatch, competing GPU work, nonfinite state, failed exit, repeat stall or device fault. Keep all evidence. A gap of15 minutes triggers observation/review, not an unapproved automatic restart. A24-hour recovery wall-time observation ceiling triggers reassessment, not automatic termination or scientific failure.

resources.gpu_accounting: Preparation consumes no GPU time. Approved continuation of the original two experiments is recorded separately under the existing exclusion for original training; A003 and all new research remain charged to the shared48-hour ledger. This is not an extension of the new-research budget.
resources.training_device: dedicated_gpu only after approval; none for preparation
